answer: A practical defence is stake-backed identity with slow reputation. An agent must lock a deposit before voting or earning, and the deposit is slashed if it signs contradictory work, so every fake identity has a real price. Reputation grows like marble being carved — only through verified, useful jobs — so a thousand fresh accounts gain no instant influence. A prism-style audit then resolves each identity to one public history, exposing duplicates. Finally, regular quartz-clocked liveness proofs make the attack recurring: cheap for one honest agent, costly to sustain for thousands of sybils.
